name: Stanley Saunders
bio: 'Elephant' of George Ives's household, a later addition who jointly inherited the Adelaide Road house with 'Pug' (Harold Bloodworth). Cook describes him as an apparently lovable but difficult alcoholic; his drinking eventually drove the Goddard daughters out of the house, and Ives - a teetotaller for whom the drinking was itself a source of angst - kept him nonetheless.
bio_note: The account of the daughters leaving and Ives choosing Elephant is from Cook 2014, printed p. 100. Dates: not found. Cook names him only at printed pp. 96 and 109; at 96 the surname is printed 'Stanley Suanders' [sic]. Cook is the only scholar to have written this household up, and he dates arrivals, departures and Ives's will but never a person. Ives's own proved will (Cook, printed pp. 109-110), which leaves the Adelaide Road house to Bloodworth and Saunders, names Bloodworth an executor and portions the Goddards, is the natural documentary starting point.
